messages.task:
You are a financial reasoning assistant. Your task is to answer the user’s question by thoughtfully analysing the scenario below and, when useful, invoking the available tools. Combine the information these tools return with your own reasoning to arrive at one concise, checkable answer.

Scenario (background information – no need to quote back):
A media company discusses its share-repurchase programme and presents a stock-performance graph that compares cumulative total shareholder return (TSR) of its three classes of common stock (Series A ― ticker DISCA, Series B ― DISCB, Series C ― DISCK) with the S&P 500 index and a peer-group index.  The narrative states that $100 invested on December 31 2008 in each security (and in the two indices) grows with reinvested dividends through to December 31 2013.  Specific numerical values for each year-end are contained in internal records that you can access only through the available tools.

Tools you may call:
• get_security_id_by_ticker(ticker) → int
  Returns the internal numeric identifier of the security whose ticker symbol is given.

• list_year_end_dates_for_security(security_id) → List[str]
  Gives all recorded year-end dates (ISO format YYYY-MM-DD) for the specified security, sorted chronologically.

• get_year_end_value(security_id, year) → float
  Provides the TSR index value (dollar amount of the $100 investment) for the given security at 31-Dec-<year>.

• compute_percent_change(start_value, end_value) → float
  Calculates the percentage change between two numeric values.

Additional exploration tools also exist (list_all_tickers, get_sector_of_security, list_indices, list_constituents_of_index, list_corporate_actions). They may help you inspect the database but are not strictly required for every query.

Question:
What was the percentage cumulative total shareholder return on DISCA for the five-year period ended December 31 2013?

Please think step-by-step, call tools as needed, and give the final answer as a single percentage value rounded to two decimal places followed by the % sign.
